identityTradability.exchangeName: Okta, Inc. - Class A Common Stock

source-integrity.name: provenance and freshness
source-integrity.basis: Primary operating evidence is current through 2026-08-27 and independent market evidence through 2026-09-26; issuer claims are not counted as independent corroboration.

structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Identity/authentication remains required across workforce, customer and emerging non-human access paths.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Identity need persists across cloud/AI scenarios, but vendor share can shift to bundled suites or competing identity platforms.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: The function is hard to eliminate; Okta-specific economics are substitutable through Microsoft and other integrated security/identity stacks.

discovery-weak-signals.name: identity-security demand
discovery-weak-signals.basis: RPO/cRPO growth and new-product contribution indicate continuing demand beyond the legacy core.

discovery-weak-signals.name: agentic-AI security adjacency
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Okta is extending identity controls to AI agents, an emerging non-human identity surface.

adversarial-red-team.name: trustConcentration
adversarial-red-team.basis: Identity security vendors are attractive attack targets and historical incidents have had reputational/customer effects.

adversarial-red-team.name: competitiveResponse
adversarial-red-team.basis: Larger established platforms can bundle identity with broader security/productivity estates.

adversarial-red-team.name: confidenceInflation
adversarial-red-team.basis: cRPO and AI-agent adjacency support execution signals but do not prove durable share or monetization.

expectations-execution.name: profitability conversion
expectations-execution.basis: Higher GAAP operating margin and cash flow show improving economic execution alongside growth.

expectations-execution.name: forward demand conversion
expectations-execution.basis: cRPO growth above current revenue growth suggests contracted near-term subscription demand, subject to normal recognition/conversion risks.

thesisQuality.basis: Identity is a durable security control plane with $4.858b RPO and expanding products, but vendor-specific moat is moderated by suite competition and trust sensitivity.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue grew 11%, cRPO 14%, GAAP operating margin reached 13% versus 6%, and Q2 free cash flow was $227m.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Current valuation is demanding relative to roughly 10-11% FY27 revenue growth guidance.

catalystScore.basis: Q3 execution, cRPO conversion and emerging AI-agent identity adoption are identifiable catalysts, but monetization remains uncertain.

governancePower.basis: Founder-led continuity and improving profitability are constructive, while historical trust/security exposure keeps evidence in the adequate-to-strong range.

alignment2036.basis: Human and non-human identities require authentication, authorization and governance as cloud and AI-agent deployment expands.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Workforce Identity, Customer Identity, governance and agent identity reuse a common identity-control capability across multiple demand surfaces.

bottleneckControl.basis: Identity/authentication is a required control point for digital access and Okta has substantial contracted demand, though competing stacks prevent unique bottleneck status.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Identity demand persists across cloud and AI scenarios, but customer consolidation into bundled platforms and security incidents can shift vendor economics.

substitutionResilience.basis: Identity controls are difficult to eliminate, but Okta-specific functionality can be substituted by integrated security/identity platforms.

supplyChainResilience.basis: The subscription-software model has little direct physical input dependence; cash resources support resilience while third-party infrastructure remains a dependency.

pricingPower.basis: Subscription economics, 13% GAAP operating margin and strong FCF margin show value capture, but bundled competition limits exceptional pricing power.

riskEvidence.basis: Material risks are demanding valuation, security/trust failure, bundled competition, AI-agent monetization uncertainty and slowing top-line growth.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity/tradability, operating results and balance-sheet facts are primary-source supported and valuation is current and independently sourced; confidence is reduced for future AI-agent economics and competitive share.

scoreRecord.thesis: Okta occupies a durable identity-control layer with improving profitability and contracted demand, while suite competition, trust sensitivity and a demanding valuation cap conviction.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A security/trust failure or bundled competitive response weakens retention and pricing while valuation leaves limited room for disappointment.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 FY2027 results and evidence that cRPO acceleration and AI-agent identity products convert into sustained revenue and cash-flow growth.

items.risk: AI-agent security is an emerging market; category importance does not establish Okta's eventual share or monetization.
Large-platform competition and customer optimization can pressure growth even with improving margins.

Successor bottleneck shifts from identity necessity to trust, integration quality and security reliability; a provider-specific breach can weaken the very control-plane trust that creates strategic value.
A material identity-platform security incident can impair trust, renewals and brand disproportionately to ordinary SaaS failures.
Bundled identity/security offerings can pressure standalone pricing and customer acquisition.
Valuation, security/trust failure, bundled competition and growth deceleration remain material.
